title: Quantum Codes for Generalized Amplitude-damping Noise
authors: Sourav Dutta, Anubhab Rudra, Manav Seksaria, Anil Prabhakar, Prabha Mandayam
abstract: Quantum error correcting (QEC) plays a crucial role in protecting quantum information against decoherence and enabling scalable, reliable quantum computing. One of the most realistic and ubiquitous sources of noise affecting quantum hardware today is generalized amplitude-damping (GAD) noise. Conventional, deterministic QEC codes struggle to correct for GAD noise because of their inherent structure, leading to fidelity losses that scale linearly with the damping strength. In this work, we introduce the framework of probabilistic approximate quantum error correction (PAQEC), that combines the flexibility of approximate QEC with the potential of post-selected recovery, enabling high-fidelity, resource-efficient error correction. We construct a five-qubit permutation-invariant code that, under probabilistic recovery, achieves a fidelity loss quadratic in the damping strength, thus outperforming existing QEC codes. Formulating PAQEC as an optimization problem, we present a numerical technique based on Charnes-Cooper and semidefinite programming to identify the optimal recovery map for any PAQEC code. Our results establish PAQEC as a powerful tool for developing resource-efficient, high-fidelity quantum codes tailored to realistic noise, with promising implications for near-term quantum devices and future fault-tolerant architectures.
summary: This work develops the Probabilistic Approximate Quantum Error Correction (PAQEC) framework to combat Generalized Amplitude-damping (GAD) noise. By optimizing recovery maps using semidefinite programming, the authors construct a five-qubit code that achieves superior, quadratic scaling of fidelity loss compared to existing methods. This offers a resource-efficient path toward building reliable quantum computers for near-term devices.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of protecting quantum information from Generalized Amplitude-damping (GAD) noise, a realistic source of decoherence, using Quantum Error Correcting (QEC) codes.
main_result: The authors introduce Probabilistic Approximate Quantum Error Correction (PAQEC) and demonstrate a five-qubit code that achieves a fidelity loss quadratic in the damping strength, significantly outperforming conventional codes.
method: The framework combines approximate QEC with post-selection recovery, formulated and optimized using numerical techniques based on Charnes–Cooper and semidefinite programming.
model_or_system: The system involves qubits subjected to GAD noise, modeled by specific Kraus operators involving damping strength ($\gamma$) and temperature-dependent parameters ($p$). The core structure is a five-qubit permutation-invariant code.
key_observables: Entanglement fidelity ($F_{	ext{ent}}$), probability of successful recovery, and the scaling of fidelity loss with noise strength.
important_parameters: Damping strength ($\gamma$), temperature-related parameter ($p$), and the noise parameters $(\gamma', p')$ used during optimization.
main_assumptions: Conventional deterministic QEC codes fail to correct for first-order GAD errors; the PAQEC framework is proposed to overcome these limitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the action of GAD errors on codewords, the syndrome-based recovery protocol using ancilla qubits, and comparisons showing the numerical code outperforming the standard PI code in fidelity.
paper_structure: The paper surveys existing AQEC/PQEC methods and GAD noise, introduces the five-qubit PI code, formally defines PAQEC conditions, and finally uses semidefinite programming to find optimal recovery maps and codes.
why_interesting: The focus on GAD noise, which is highly relevant to superconducting and trapped-ion quantum hardware, provides a concrete, realistic noise model for developing fault-tolerant quantum computation protocols.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Action of generalized amplitude-damping on the [5,1] PI code. A first-order GAD error G(a) m maps codeword ∣iL⟩into a state in the subspace S(a) i . Subspaces {S(a) i }i,a are mutually orthogonal for different i and a. Note that the codespace overlaps with S(0) 0 and S(0) 1 .
FIG. 2: Syndrome-based recovery protocol for the [5,1] PI code. Circuit for syndrome-based recovery of the five-qubit permutation-invariant code under GAD noise.

FIG. 3: Performance of [5,1] PI code. (a) Entanglement fidelity as a function of noise parameters γ and p, for the [5,1] PI code and the [5,1,3] stabilizer code with a numerically optimized recovery. (b) Average probability of successful recovery as a function of γ, with 0 ≤p ≤0.5, for the [5,1] PI code.

FIG. 4: Performance of different noise-adapted recoveries, for the [5,1] PI code. Entanglement fidelity versus the damping strength γ for (a) p = 0.05 and (b) p = 0.2, for the [5,1] permutation-invariant code with different noise-adapted recoveries, the [5,1,3] code (numerically optimized recovery), and the bare qubit.

FIG. 5: Performance comparison of the [5,1] PI code and the numerically optimized code. (a) Entanglement fidelity vs. γ. (b) Recovery probability vs. γ. The numerical code outperforms the PI code at p = 0.05. This improvement comes at the cost of a lower probability of success (increased overhead).
